basis: Lymphatic vascular dysplasia causes impaired drainage; varicose veins and atrial septal defects support the cardiovascular axis. Edema alone does not establish skin damage.
Vitamin deficiency is a metabolic disorder; rickets and osteomalacia are separately diagnosed consequences, not universal features.
Hypophosphatemia, hyperparathyroidism and rickets define the disorder. Hormone-driven phosphate wasting does not itself establish kidney damage.
Autoimmune bilateral granulomatous uveitis. Hearing impairment and cutaneous manifestations occur in only 5-29%.
Intraosseous venous malformations deform bone; gingival bleeding and ectopic teeth occur in 8/8, visual loss in 5/6. Anemia is secondary to bleeding.
Developmental impairment defines the syndrome; cardiac malformations occur in 80-99%, kyphoscoliosis/chest deformity in 30-79%. GH deficiency is deletion-subtype dependent.
Dermatosis affects eyelid skin; both eyelid and cutaneous axes apply. No specific immune mechanism is established.
The specified primary site is vulva, a reproductive organ. Neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease; cutaneous Merkel carcinoma is a subtype.
A teratoma histologic category, usually gonadal, without a specified site in an eligible axis. Extragonadal organ involvement cannot be inferred.
Hereditary corticospinal disease causes spastic paraplegia and developmental motor impairment. Weakness and stiffness reflect neural dysfunction.
Collapsing glomerular injury and nephrotic protein loss define this kidney disease; idiopathic steroid resistance does not establish immune mediation.
A psychiatric mood disorder without defining direct damage to an eligible organ axis.
Thrombocytopenia and glomerulonephritis define the syndrome. Elevated IgA alone does not establish autoimmune disease or immunodeficiency.
Chronic immune-mediated pustular skin disease. Associated psoriatic arthritis and thyroid dysfunction are separate diseases.
Skeletal and hair/nail defects with nephronophthisis define the syndrome; dental defects occur in 80-99%. Hepatic fibrosis and retinal disease omitted at the four-axis cap.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease. Otitis occurs in 1/11; situs inversus and dextrocardia alone do not imply cardiac damage.
Myopathy with defining ptosis/ophthalmoplegia in 7/7; leukoencephalopathy and ataxia occur in 3/6. Dysphagia reflects muscle weakness; retinopathy occurs in 2/7.
Deficiency of an anticoagulant protein is a coagulation disorder. Thrombosis is a separately diagnosed complication, not established vascular damage in every carrier.
Defined by autoimmune destruction or dysfunction of blood components.
Congenital anomalous coronary artery origin and course directly involve the cardiovascular system.
Gastric mucosal overgrowth causes protein-losing gastropathy. Hypoalbuminemia and edema are consequences; H. pylori is an associated separate infection.
Inherited retinal dystrophy causes severe congenital visual dysfunction; no extraocular damage is established.
Intellectual disability, developmental delay, ataxia and spasticity define a neurodevelopmental disorder. No independent metabolic phenotype is established.
Inherited enzyme/metabolic defects produce skeletal stippling and dysplasia. Skin and ocular disease vary by subtype; common involvement across the umbrella is not established.
Syndromic intellectual disability; brachydactyly/joint abnormalities and cardiac malformations each occur in 30-79%. Renal ectopia and intestinal malrotation occur in 5-29%.
